rationale: Recorded the current account for receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce, which executes the durability discriminator on a three-voter committed configuration: the restarted former leader reconstructed one voter against the three in its own log (comparison 0 violated, valid witness at parsed index 22; control holds at 24), and the commit it acknowledged existed on exactly one copy of the committed configuration's members, the other two voters forming new leadership without ever receiving it (comparison 2 violated at parsed index 22; control holds at 24, where the flag-disabled restart acknowledged nothing). Added a durability fact, extended the reconstruction fact with this third ladder, kept the repair gap open and pointed the discriminator at the live-cluster repair question.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a healthy leader's ordinary replication repairs the stale reconstruction of a restarted follower that stays in the cluster (its log already matching the leader's), and whether a later configuration entry appended by that leader does repair it.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across three ladders: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; and the three-voter ladder reported one voter against the three-voter entry at log index 106. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); no membership change is issued after the restart.
knowledge.changed_premise: Adds the three-voter ladder observed in receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce, where the reconstructed configuration is smaller again (one voter against three) and the commit acknowledged under it is the case the durability predicates rest on; the measured divergence direction is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-voter execution, a commit acknowledged to the client rested on a single copy of the committed configuration: the restarted instance's Apply completed (acknowledged true, payload index 113) while only it held that payload (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1, durable_on_majority false), the two other voters reconstructed their own three-voter configuration and elected new leadership without it, and after the holder rejoined the payload was still present only there (payload_on_holder_after_rejoin true at index 113) with the new leadership formed in the same term as the stale leader (both 3).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster whose committed configuration entry sits at log index 106 while the restarted instance's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; every instance is stopped before the restart, the restarted instance is the only running member when it acknowledges the commit, the other two voters are then rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled, and the payload is searched for in every store across its first-to-last index.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed, 25 parsed events) closes the durability part of the question on a three-voter committed configuration. Reconstruction: comparison 0 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 22, where the restarted former leader held reconstructed_config_voters 1 while its own log's configuration entry at index 106 has three voters, and comparison 1 holds at parsed index 24, where the flag-disabled restart reconstructed three voters; the lost_inputs events at parsed indices 21 and 23 record the committed three-voter configuration at log index 106 against snapshot metadata carrying one voter. Durability: comparison 2 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 22, where the instance's Apply completed (acknowledged true, payload_index 113) yet the payload existed on exactly one copy of the committed configuration's members (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1, durable_on_majority false), the other two voters having reconstructed their own three-voter configuration, elected leadership among themselves and never received it; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 24, where the flag-disabled restart could not be a leader of the committed three-voter configuration with only itself running, so no commit was acknowledged at all ("node is not the leader") and nothing single-copy could be created. Mechanism: the reconstructed configurations.latest is what runFollower's eligibility branch, quorumSize for the candidacy and the leader commitment are computed from [follower_gate, candidate_quorum, quorum_size, leader_commitment, commitment_impl], and its divergence traces to the startup scan skipping the committed configuration entry [scan_start, restore_lastapplied]. Together with receipt faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1 (two-voter committed configuration: leadership with no election request and a completed commit while the other committed voter was stopped, comparisons holding at parsed indices 16, 17, 19 and 20) and receipt 63d4401225884bdd9c75fbe580336c63 (empty and stale reconstructions with reproducible bounded non-progress), the account is that RestoreCommittedLogs restarts can reconstruct a support basis the committed configuration does not sanction, bounded below by non-progress and above by client-acknowledged decisions resting on a minority of the committed configuration. Countervailing detail specific to this receipt: the acknowledged copy was not discarded during the observation, it stayed on the holder at index 113 after the holder rejoined, and the new leadership was elected in the same term as the stale leader (both 3), so what is established is a single-copy acknowledgement, not an erased entry; losing the acknowledged decision would additionally require the holder's own state to be lost, which this harness cannot express. The repair question stays open and is answered only from source so far: the other two voters never received the entry through ordinary replication while the holder's configuration stayed reconstructed [append_new].
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces the divergence and the non-progress: excluded by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same decisions.

The acknowledged payload survived on its holder in this receipt (payload_on_holder_after_rejoin true at index 113) and the new leadership formed in the same term, so no entry was erased; the consequence is that the acknowledgement was never durable on a majority, not that the entry is shown to be gone.
limitations: Single process with in-memory stores; the durability failure is shown as an absent majority copy, not as an unrecoverable loss of the holder's state.

The two voters brought back after the acknowledged commit were deliberately restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so that their own configuration comes from their logs; their leadership therefore exercises the correct configuration, which is what makes the payload's absence observable.
The acknowledged commit is a single payload acknowledged in one leadership window; no rate, repetition or longer-sequence claim follows.
The repair question remains unexecuted, and disk-backed stores, crashes during the restart and post-restart membership changes are still not exercised.
